# Noisy Local Certification

Scientific question: determine the copy cost of testing a fully known generic pure quantum target when each input qubit yields one destructive noisy local report.

## Authoritative reading routes

- Model, promises, resources and result map: science/model-and-results.md
- Uniform centered product-effect concentration with explicit finite constants: science/uniform-concentration.md
- Complete adaptive/interleaved transcript converse, exact Haar moments and matching binary exponent: science/binary-sample-law.md
- Exact-target and gap-compatible robust fidelity certification, classical score inversion and polynomial noise budget: science/fidelity-certification.md
- Approximate state designs, polynomial preparation cost and charged inverse control: science/circuit-targets.md
- Detector versus acquisition noise, separable/global measurements and paid redundancy: science/acquisition-and-control.md
- Prior work and inherited ingredients: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/REFERENCES.md
- Reproduction commands, numerical scope and input hashes: code/README.md and results/verification.json

## Essential distinctions

The optimal exponential rate is for known-target versus maximally-mixed binary testing, not a matched general-fidelity exponent. The fidelity threshold has exact-target completeness or an explicit gap-dependent robust promise. Haar typicality does not imply hardness for every target. The binary design extension does not automatically transfer the ideal full-fidelity verification gap. Classical computation is unrestricted and can be exponential. Copies may be interleaved; the cap counts all attempted copies. Repeated QND reports, ancilla redundancy and coherent processing are additional resources. Detector noise after clean control and depolarization before control are different models.

This guide maps scientific questions to source files. It does not replace proofs, grant permissions or claim indexing.
